doc.title: Tom Lellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 31, 2007

title: Record labels and goodbyes
summary: He says labels did not help him as much as his own Beamtide label album, and the interview ends with thanks.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: I’m glad to be able to do that. Does it help to have a record label these days?

I don’t know that it does. Because I was on Concord, I was on Inner City, I was on Adventure Music, and I didn’t see any — I worked more when I put out my first album on Beamtide, my label, with Jack DeJohnette and Eddie Gomez, “Double Entendre.” I worked for a year and a half on that album all over the country, all over the world, and yet with the albums on labels things weren’t really that great, no. I don’t know. As I say, I think as the quality goes down the singers of quality or the musicians of quality have a harder time because the level is so low that everybody can do it.
Right. Well not everybody can do what you do.
Well anyway, it’s been a great pleasure talking with you.
Oh, thank you, man. A pleasure, totally.
